status: a candidate enters arithmetic, spans and declared comparisons only with a current supported receipt in CANDIDATE_SUPPORT_REVIEW.json
selection_rule: Registered publishers (IEA, LBNL, EPRI, McKinsey, Goldman Sachs, BloombergNEF, S&P Global with 451 Research, Deloitte and Gartner) were searched on 9 October 2026 for publications dated after the 8 October 2026 currency sweep. Two editions from other publishers were added at the author's decision of 9 October 2026: TrendForce's press release of 16 September 2026 and AEMO's 2026 data-centre forecast with Oxford Economics Australia, published in August 2026. A figure is registered only where the publisher's own retained publication states a value with a target year, unit and geography that the ledger's fields can hold; a financial-year target is recorded under the source's own year label, with the financial-year basis stated. Other values in the same publications are listed as known unregistered values. Candidates await independent claim-support receipts and enter no arithmetic until a supported receipt is bound. The sample remains a convenience sample of named institutions, not a census. Non-US addition, at the author's request of 11 October 2026, under a rule declared and recorded before the new originals were retrieved: European geographies first, from the registered publishers' European figures and from European public bodies and transmission system operators, then China; a figure only from the forecasting body's own retained publication dated 2025 or 2026 that states a value with a target year, unit and geography the ledger's fields can hold, the 2030 value where one is stated; the base, central, reference or median case, or else the case the publication presents as its headline, with its name; each publisher's own definition of the geography; a figure stated only in another organisation's publication is a lead, not registered. Settled after retrieval, because the rule left them open: a publisher's latest edition is registered and an earlier edition's figure listed as a known unregistered value, because a candidate carries no supersession; where a publication states both annual electricity and capacity for 2030, the annual electricity value is registered, as the ledger does for the IEA; a publication that names no central case but presents two retained trajectories is registered as the range across them, as the ledger records EPRI's scenario range. Version 0.5, under a rule frozen on 15 October 2026 at 05:00:47 BST before new originals were retrieved (RULE_AND_COVERAGE_PROTOCOL_0.5.md): the same rules, applied to the in-scope items of the 0.4 coverage record and to a window search of 12 to 15 October 2026, for publications dated up to and including 15 October 2026. Where a publisher refused automated retrieval, the author saved the publication in an ordinary browser and the saved file is the retained original. An increment from a base year, which the ledger's fields cannot hold, is listed as a known unregistered value (the author's decision of 15 October 2026). The completion of the window search on 17 October 2026, under the same rules, found four publications dated before the cut-off that the rules admit, which the author added to version 0.5 on 17 October 2026: PSE's network development plan (Poland), NVE's method note (Norway), the report for Germany's federal economics ministry and the study for Switzerland's Federal Office of Energy. At the same decision, a study commissioned and published by a public body counts as that body's publication, as the coverage record of 15 October 2026 counted the European Commission's commissioned reports, and a case the publication names its best guess counts as its central case.

records.locator: Press release of 16 September 2026, section on the 2030 global supply-demand capacity gap, second paragraph, first sentence
records.qualification: N01 states the registered value as global data-centre power demand capacity projected for 2030 and divides demand capacity into general servers, AI servers, other IT equipment and non-IT equipment such as cooling and power supply systems, so the boundary includes facility overhead. N01's retained text and its retained article image name no scenario and no data-centre types and do not mention cryptocurrency. TrendForce's 22 September 2026 article (N04) describes the demand line as fleet electricity use converted into power capacity; a note on one of its charts states that TrendForce's line uses a conversion consistent with IEA public data and that LBNL equates its 2030 Reference Case to 148 GW of interconnection capacity at 50% utilisation, and N04's retained text and article images give no number for TrendForce's conversion. No 2030 figure occurs in the retained text or retained article image of TrendForce's earlier release N05, so no earlier TrendForce vintage of this quantity is registered. Other values in N01 are listed as NK01, NK02 and NK10. The underlying report is not retained.
records.method_description: AI server industry research (N01); demand capacity grouped by equipment type, with the non-IT category labelled PUE-derived in the release's chart (N01); shipment estimates accumulated into the fleet in service, whose annual electricity use is converted into power capacity on a basis N04 describes as consistent with IEA public data, with no number given (N04); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

records.forecast_vintage: 2026 forecast update (2026 Electricity Statement of Opportunities)
records.locator: Page of 25 August 2026, summary paragraph on the Step Change scenario, FY30 value
records.qualification: N03 presents Oxford Economics Australia's and AEMO's joint forecast. The target is labelled FY30, a financial year rather than a calendar year; neither N02 nor N03 states the months of the financial year. The value is for the National Electricity Market, which N02 describes as supplying eastern and south-eastern Australia; the national value is listed as NK05. AEMO's own overview (N02) reports the same value approximately and states it as a share of forecast operational consumption (NK09), and describes Step Change as its most likely scenario (printed 'mostly likely'). Neither page states a facility boundary or mentions cryptocurrency. Other scenarios are listed as NK07 and the stated revision from the 2025 forecast as NK08.
records.method_description: Joint forecast combining a project approach with probabilistic weighting of prospective projects and an economic approach with a logistic electricity-intensity curve and an international demand component (N03); N02 describes project-level information from developers and network service providers combined with an economic outlook; published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

RTE names no central case: it studies three deliberately contrasting trajectories, décarbonation rapide, built as an update of the 2023 edition's A - référence scenario, décarbonation lente, and a stagnation trajectory studied as a sensitivity test, which for data centres assumes very slow growth to 2030 without a stated value; for data centres it retained the first two after public consultation, and the range spans them. records.method_description: Trajectories built from the power of data-centre projects with a signed connection offer, aggregated by planned connection year, with assumed concretisation rates, a ramp-up of the order of ten years and the maximum power reached: in the décarbonation rapide trajectory, about 60% concretisation (4.3 GW) of transmission-connected projects due before 2030, an average utilisation of 20% of connection capacity at that horizon and about 2.4 TWh of growth from distribution-connected sites; in the décarbonation lente trajectory, about 30% concretisation and about 1.8 TWh of distribution growth (N08 sections 2.5.2 and 2.5.3); published outputs read; model not rebuilt.

AF25 is a target-fulfilment scenario: its base course is in principle compatible with meeting the political climate and energy targets, though not all of them are directly reflected. The included data centres range from about 1 MW to hyperscale sites of 150 MW or more. N09 states that AF25 has markedly lower consumption than AF24 in the short term and higher consumption in the long term.
